text: Explain how the Node.js event loop works. Why is Node.js suitable for I/O-bound tasks but not CPU-bound tasks?
referenceAnswer: Node.js runs on a single thread but uses libuv's event loop to handle asynchronous I/O without blocking. When an async operation (file read, network request) is initiated, it is offloaded to the OS/thread pool. When complete, the callback is pushed to the event queue and executed by the event loop. This makes Node ideal for I/O-bound tasks (many concurrent connections) because threads aren't blocked. However, CPU-heavy computation blocks the single thread, preventing other requests from being served — use worker threads or offload to microservices for CPU-bound work.

rubric.criterion: Explains why CPU tasks block the loop
Suggests worker threads or offloading for CPU tasks

text: Describe the React component lifecycle and how hooks replace lifecycle methods. Include useEffect in your answer.
referenceAnswer: Class components have lifecycle methods: componentDidMount (after first render), componentDidUpdate (after re-render), componentWillUnmount (cleanup). Hooks replace these in functional components. useEffect with an empty dependency array [] mimics componentDidMount. With a dependency array it runs when those values change (componentDidUpdate). Returning a cleanup function from useEffect mimics componentWillUnmount. useState replaces this.state.

rubric.criterion: Explains useEffect with empty array = componentDidMount

text: Explain what indexes are in MongoDB and when you should and should not use them.
referenceAnswer: Indexes in MongoDB are data structures (B-tree by default) that store a small portion of the collection's data in an easy-to-traverse form. They speed up read queries dramatically by avoiding full collection scans. Use indexes on fields frequently used in queries, sort operations, or join-like lookups. Avoid over-indexing: each index consumes memory and slows write operations (insert/update/delete must update all indexes). Compound indexes cover multiple fields. The explain() method helps identify missing indexes.

rubric.criterion: Explains B-tree or avoids full scan
Knows when to use indexes (frequent query fields)

text: What is the difference between deep learning and traditional machine learning? When would you choose one over the other?
referenceAnswer: Traditional ML (e.g. SVM, Random Forest) requires manual feature engineering — domain experts extract relevant features from raw data. Deep learning (neural networks) learns feature representations automatically from raw data. Choose traditional ML when data is small/tabular and interpretability matters. Choose deep learning for large datasets, unstructured data (images, text, audio), and when high accuracy outweighs interpretability and compute cost.

rubric.criterion: Traditional ML requires manual feature engineering
Traditional ML preferred for small/tabular data
Deep learning preferred for unstructured/large data

text: Explain the concept of containerisation using Docker. How is a container different from a virtual machine?
referenceAnswer: Containerisation packages an application with its dependencies into a container image so it runs consistently across environments. Docker uses the host OS kernel (via Linux namespaces and cgroups) rather than emulating hardware. VMs run a full OS on a hypervisor, consuming more memory and taking longer to start. Containers are lightweight (MB vs GB), start in seconds, and share the host kernel. VMs offer stronger isolation; containers offer better density and portability.

rubric.criterion: VMs run a full OS on hypervisor

text: Describe the MVC (Model-View-Controller) design pattern and explain how it is implemented in an Express.js application.
referenceAnswer: MVC separates an application into three layers. Model: handles data logic and DB interaction (Mongoose schemas in Express). View: presents data to the user (JSON responses in an API; HTML in a full-stack app). Controller: receives HTTP requests, calls the Model, and returns a response. In Express: routes define URL patterns → controllers handle business logic → models query MongoDB. This separation makes the codebase maintainable and testable.
